analysis.title: Oil Strategy Weekly Physical: The Freight Factor
key_insights: Freight rates have become a dominant variable in physical crude pricing. They rose sharply as a share of total delivered crude prices and, despite easing from recent highs, remain elevated.
Elevated freight and competition from other grades are hurting arbitrage viability for many Atlantic Basin grades. With limited near-term solutions, RBC says the factor could linger for some time.
Multi-front conflicts have caused logistical inefficiencies and added risk premiums to freight. Long-haul economics suffer most, so shorter-range and local alternatives have been more attractive.
FOB prices for key Atlantic Basin regions such as WAF and LATAM have rerated lower to accommodate the high freight rates, which has reshaped regional pricing differentials.
WAF differentials have improved off record lows of past weeks but have struggled to gain footing because other grades are competitive in Europe and Asia.
Rates have come off their most untenable levels of recent weeks, but freight still continues to impede differential strength.
risk_factors: Freight rates could stay elevated, since there are limited viable near-term solutions.
Continued multi-front conflicts could keep logistical inefficiencies and freight risk premiums in place.
Competition from other grades in Europe and Asia could keep WAF differentials weak.
geopolitical: Multi-front conflicts are driving logistical inefficiencies in trade and risk premiums on freight, per the report.
